Hi Jordan 

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of what I heard and a couple of clarifying questions so we can build a recommendation and initial quota proposal: 

Summary from call:
- Target 95th pct latency: <= 250ms for single-request text-generation (avg request size ~120 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target: ~450 requests/min across your fleet during business hours (US daytime).
- Bursty concurrency: up to 80 parallel simultaneous requests during peak events.
- Streaming: yes  you need chunked/streaming responses for chat UX; target first-byte <= 120ms when streaming enabled.
- Connection handling: you plan to use connection pooling from your API gateway (keep-alives), ~200 open connections from a single region.

Clarifying questions:
1) Are the 80 parallel requests per customer session or total across Acme's org? (I believe you said total across the org.)
2) For streaming, are you okay with a small warmup window where first requests may be ~2x latency for KV cache population?
3) Any hard regulatory constraints on retries or fallback copies?

Proposed next steps:
- If you confirm Q1	6Q3, Ill put together a short quota proposal (concurrency slots + token throughput + rate limits) and expected cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted with reserved capacity.
- Quick follow-up call next week to walk the proposal and map to your SLOs. I included a 30-min booking link below.

Attachments: acme-performance-requirements.pdf (your doc from today)

Thanks  talk soon.

Hi Marissa 

Thanks for the clear recap  that looks right. Answers below:

1) The 80 parallel requests are total across Acme (all services combined) originating from our region-1 cluster. We expect them to concentrate around 1011am PT.
2) Warmup window is fine; we can tolerate the occasional 2x latency on cache miss for the first few requests during a burst. We want to avoid consistent cold starts.
3) No unusual regulatory constraints on retries, but we limit client-side retries to 1 retry per request; server-side we'd prefer deterministic throttling and 429 behavior.

One more data point: our average request payload is 140 tokens (input+expected output), and we estimate ~1.1M tokens/day across all workloads.

I attached the performance requirements doc (acme-performance-requirements.pdf). Happy to review a proposed quota plan.

Jordan 

Appreciate the quick answers and the doc. We put together an initial quota recommendation and a short summary of how Redwood enforces rate limits  see inline bullets below and I can send a formal quote after you confirm these numbers.

Initial recommendation (conservative):
- Reserved concurrency slots: 90 total (gives 10% headroom above 80 peak).
- Connection guidance: keep-alive pooling, recommend max 8 requests per connection; with 200 connections that maps to ~1600 logical parallel inflight capacity  but we'll size concurrency slots based on expected active requests, not open sockets.
- Token rate: 1.2M tokens/day provisioned (10% headroom). Equivalent to ~14 tokens/sec sustained on average, but we express as per-minute limits in the proposal.
- Burst policy: token-bucket with a 60s burst window allowing up to 2x sustained rate for short spikes; after burst is exhausted, requests are metered and may get 429s if over quota.
- Streaming: prioritized routing to low-latency pool for first-byte SLO; streaming sessions consume concurrency slots per active session.

Redwood rate-limit behavior (summary):
- Per-API-key rate limits applied at regional egress point.
- Soft limits (warning) emitted at 80% utilization; hard limits return 429 with Retry-After.
- We support graceful fallbacks: routing to a smaller model variant automatically when capacity constrained (if you opt in).

Next steps:
1) Confirm you’re comfortable with the 10% headroom on concurrency and token provisioning.
2) If confirmed, I’ll send a formal quote with Hosted vs Dedicated pricing and a suggested SLA for the Dedicated pool.
3) We can schedule a technical walk-through with our SREs to validate warmup behavior and streaming latency in a short perf test.

Booking link: https://cal.com/marissa/30min

If that sounds good I’ll get the quote over today.
